2288263.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality across South Tripura District and adjoining areas in the State of Tripura under North East LSA
2288263.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality across South Tripura District and adjoining areas in the State of Tripura under North East LSA
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across South Tripura District and adjoining areas in the State of Tripura under North East LSA, during the month of May 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 244.2 KMs, Hotspot locations - 9, Walk Test – 1.6 KMs in Tripura State during 13th May 2026 to 16th May 2026 in North East LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Kolkata. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Services: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

           

The overall mobile network performance in South Tripura District and adjoining areas for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

a)    Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the city drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 6217/ 30754 for Airtel, 11854/ 28800 for BSNL, 7590/ 35527 for RJIL and 8627/ 19553 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

 

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 9/ 221 for Airtel, 22/ 176 for BSNL, 2/ 254 for RJIL and 24/ 148 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

 

c)    Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 17/ 201 for Airtel, 24/ 131 for BSNL, 20/ 244 for RJIL and 6/ 99 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

 

d)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

 

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 88.67  Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 10.64 Mbps for BSNL (4G/2G), 46.11 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 35.19 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

 

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 17.32 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 3.25 Mbps for BSNL (4G/ 2G), 3.83 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 6.84 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

 

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

 

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: -

a)      City - The areas covered in the city drive Rajnagar, Belonia, Paikhola, Rajapur, Santirbazar, Baikhora, Jolaibari, Gardhang, Bhuratali, Manu Bazar, Kalachara, Sabroom, Baishnabpur, Dakshin Manu Bankul and Matai etc. in Cities and Adjoining areas of South Tripura District.

 

b)   Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience, are (i) Belonia Sub Post Office Bank Rd Opp. to Old Motor Stand Belonia; (ii) District Court Belonia; (iii) District Hospital Santirbazar; (iv) Iswar Chandra Vidyasagar College Belonia; (v) Jolaibari BDO Office Muhuripur R.F.; (vi) Manu H.S. School Manu Bazar; (vii) Sabroom Sub-Divisional Hospital Sabroom; (viii) The Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge Sabroom; (ix) Trishna Wild Life Sanctuary Belonia Joychandrapur.

 

c)     Walk Test - The walk tests conducted during 13th to 15th May 2026, covered (i) Sabroom Railway Station Paschim Jalefa and (ii) Sub-Division Hospital Belonia, capturing mobile network behaviour in crowded pedestrian environments.

 

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.kolkata@trai.gov.in or Regional Office of TRAI at Kolkata RO can be contacted on telephone no.  +91-33-22361401.

2288255.title: Government Strengthens Drug Demand Reduction, Expands De-Addiction Services and Streamlines Support Under Centrally Sponsored Schemes: MoS for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma in Written Reply in Lok Sabha
2288255.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Drug Demand Reduction, Expands De-Addiction Services and Streamlines Support Under Centrally Sponsored Schemes: MoS for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma in Written Reply in Lok Sabha
More Than 29.68 Crore Citizens Reached Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Through Nationwide Awareness Campaigns
Government Supports 765 De-Addiction and Rehabilitation Facilities Across the Country Under NAPDDR
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 2:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is continuously strengthening the implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes to ensure timely financial assistance, enhanced transparency and improved delivery of services in the areas of drug demand reduction, rehabilitation and social justice. The Ministry has introduced measures to simplify fund release procedures, expand de-addiction infrastructure and enhance access to rehabilitation services across the country.

This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma in a written reply to a number of questions put forth by Member of Parliament Smt Pratima Mondal

The Minister informed the House that the Department has established a stringent monitoring mechanism to ensure timely processing of proposals and release of funds under various Centrally Sponsored Schemes. A revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has also been introduced to simplify the release of grants to partner NGOs implementing schemes such as the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) and the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) by reducing documentation requirements and improving administrative efficiency.

Highlighting the Government's efforts to tackle substance abuse, Shri Verma stated that the Ministry is implementing a comprehensive and evidence-based strategy under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR). The strategy is based on the findings of the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India conducted by National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC) at AIIMS, New Delhi.

The survey estimates that alcohol remains the most widely consumed substance among adults (18 to 75 years) with approximately 15.10 crore users, followed by 2.90 crore cannabis users, 1.90 crore opioid users, 1.10 crore sedative users and 60 lakh inhalant users in this category. Among children and adolescents (10 to 17 years), the survey estimates around 40 lakh opioid users, 30 lakh alcohol users, 30 lakh inhalant users and 20 lakh cannabis users, underscoring the need for sustained awareness, prevention and treatment initiatives.

The Minister further informed that under NAPDDR, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territories, NGOs and Government hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation. At present, the Ministry supports 344 Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts (IRCAs), 45 Community-based Peer Led Interventions (CPLIs), 76 Outreach and Drop-in Centres (ODICs), 145 District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs) and 155 Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) across the country.

The written reply further stated that the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), launched on 15 August 2020 and expanded to all districts in August 2023, has emerged as one of the world's largest awareness campaigns against substance abuse.

As on date, the campaign has reached more than 29.68 crore citizens, including over 11.43 crore youth and 8.05 crore women, through nationwide awareness activities. More than 1.17 lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras have also joined the campaign to strengthen community participation. In addition, over 28.29 lakh persons have been treated and rehabilitated besides undertaking outreach activities in 21.73 lakh educational institutions across the country.

To improve accessibility to treatment services, the Ministry has launched the NMBA 2.0 Mobile Application, enabling citizens to locate the nearest de-addiction centre. During 2024-25, 55 new District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs) were approved in GAP districts, while 21 additional DDACs were established during 2025-26, further expanding the country's de-addiction infrastructure.

The Minister also informed the House that independent third-party evaluations conducted by M/s Development & Research Services Pvt. Ltd. in December 2024 and NITI Aayog in 2025 have found that the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction has made significant progress in strengthening institutional capacity and creating awareness against substance abuse across the country.

The Government continues to strengthen its commitment towards a drug-free and socially inclusive India by expanding rehabilitation infrastructure, enhancing preventive interventions, simplifying implementation procedures and ensuring efficient delivery of Centrally Sponsored Schemes. Through sustained community participation, improved governance and technology-enabled service delivery, the Ministry remains committed to protecting vulnerable communities and promoting social justice for all.

2288253.title: Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Addresses Commonwealth Sports Ministers Meeting in Glasgow, Scotland
2288253.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2288253.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Addresses Commonwealth Sports Ministers Meeting in Glasgow, Scotland
India reaffirms its commitment to safe, inclusive, and equitable sport systems that respect human rights and create opportunities for all: Dr. Mandaviya
Dr. Mandaviya Reaffirms India’s Readiness to Host the Historic 2030 Centenary Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 2:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya urged for a stronger, member-driven framework for Commonwealth sports cooperation while addressing the Commonwealth Sports Ministers Meeting in Glasgow, Scotland.

Delivering the keynote address on "Reimagining Working Together: Strengthening Commonwealth Collaboration on Sport," Dr. Mandaviya outlined India's vision for expanding collaboration in sports governance, athlete welfare and institutional capacity across the Commonwealth.

Highlighting India's long-term commitment to Commonwealth sport, the Minister said the country is preparing to host the 2030 Centenary Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.

 

“Guided by our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, we have defined a vision for a Developed India by 2047 and Sports is a vital pillar of this roadmap. As the host of the 2030 Centenary Commonwealth Games and the 13th Commonwealth Sports Ministers Meeting in Amdavad, we are committed to delivering an exceptional Games, while leaving behind a lasting institutional legacy for Commonwealth sport,” he said. 

Dr. Mandaviya also outlined the governance reforms, strengthened anti-doping framework, and flagship initiatives such as Khelo India, Fit India, and the ASMITA League, which are nurturing grassroots talent, empowering greater participation of women in sports, and fostering a vibrant sporting culture across the nation.

He expressed India's strong support for establishing a Commonwealth Sport Coordination Forum as an annual platform to translate ministerial decisions into action, alongside a network of member-led Commonwealth Centres of Excellence to promote knowledge sharing and capacity building.

"India would be pleased to host meetings, technical workshops and regional consultations in the lead-up to 2030," he said.

The Union Minister noted that the proposed member-led approach reflects India's own reforms in sports governance.

“Last year, we brought into force the National Sports Governance Act to strengthen accountability, professional governance and athlete welfare across national sports bodies," he said.

Dr. Mandaviya reaffirmed India’s readiness to host the 2030 Centenary Commonwealth Games, stating that Ahmedabad is fully prepared to deliver a historic, sustainable, and memorable edition of the Games. 

He said Ahmedabad's world-class sporting infrastructure, and commitment to excellence reflect India’s growing stature as a global sporting powerhouse and its capability to successfully host major international multi-sport events.

He also endorsed the proposed leadership model under which the incoming host nation of the Commonwealth Sports Ministers Meeting would serve as Chair, with the President of Commonwealth Sport serving as Co-Chair.

"India will be honoured to assume the Chair of CABOS for the 2026–2030 cycle," he said.

Concluding his address, Dr. Mandaviya urged Commonwealth nations to strengthen partnerships and build enduring institutions that harness the power of sport for social development.

“Let us build institutions that endure, strengthen collaboration that delivers results, and harness the transformative power of sport for future generations. India reaffirms its commitment to safe, inclusive, and equitable sport systems that respect human rights and create opportunities for all,” he added.

Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi

CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, as you might be aware, several persons have lost their lives and many have been adversely affected by heavy rains and associated disasters such as floods, lightning strikes and landslides in various parts of the country, particularly in the States of Assam, Arunachal  Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal  Pradesh, Union territory of Jammu & Kashmir, Kerala, Mizoram, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, during June and July, 2026.

The loss of precious lives and injury to people is indeed painful and unfortunate. 

The House joins me in expressing heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families and prays for the speedy recovery and rehabilitation of the injured and affected. 

I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in these natural calamities.

2288239.title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: WEATHER FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNINGS
2288239.body_html:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: WEATHER FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNINGS
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Mission Mausam was launched by the Honorable Prime Minister on 14 January 2025 with the goal of making the country, including Maharashtra, a 'Weather-ready and Climate-smart' nation. The objective of Mission Mausam is to strengthen various components of the Earth System observations, to realize Earth System approach to provide an early warning system, for seamless weather and climate services to all. The scheme seeks to exponentially enhance the country's weather and climate observations, understanding, modelling and forecasting, leading to better, more useful, accurate, and timely services. The key objectives of this Mission include:

  • Developing cutting-edge weather surveillance technologies and systems.
  • Implementing higher-resolution atmospheric observations with improved temporal and spatial sampling and coverage.
  • Deploying next-generation radars, wind profilers, and satellites equipped with advanced instrument payloads.
  • Implementing advanced high-performance computing (HPC) systems.
  • Enhancing our understanding of weather and climate processes and improving prediction capabilities.
  • Developing advanced Earth system models and data-driven methods, including the use of AI/ML
  • Creating technologies and protocols for effective weather management
  • Establishing a state-of-the-art Decision Support System (DSS) and dissemination system for last-mile connectivity
  • Strengthening capacity building and research collaborations

The current status of the observational network and modeling capability are as follows:

  • India Meteorological Department (IMD) presently receives data from a network of 50 Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs) operated by IMD and other MoES institutions and ISRO across the country. The observational network is being progressively strengthened through the deployment of 29 C-Band DWRs, 45 X-Band DWRs, and 12 S-Band DWRs across the country to enhance weather monitoring observations, numerical weather prediction, and the study of atmospheric dynamics. These initiatives are expected to significantly improve the country's observational capabilities, including those in Maharashtra. The current DWR network in Maharashtra is given in Annexure-I.
  • Under the Mission Mausam initiative, various global and regional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) modeling systems have been implemented and operationalized to provide seamless short-range, medium-range, and extended-range weather forecasts, thereby further enhancing the accuracy and reliability of weather forecasting services. There are two different frameworks of global modeling systems based on global forecast systems (GFS) of IMD and Mithuna modeling systems of NCMRWF, Noida. Both models run in real-time with a horizontal resolution of 12 km. The New Bharat Forecasting System (BharatFS) is operational at a very high resolution of 6 km to cater to block levels and further to panchayat levels. In order to provide computational support for such high-resolution models and to make it regularly run in real time, the computing facilities have also been substantially increased with computational power to integrate voluminous data and to run mesoscale, regional, and global models at higher resolution. The "Arunika" supercomputing system at the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF), Noida, and the "Arka" system at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, have significantly enhanced the Ministry of Earth Sciences' overall high-performance computing capacity.

The Ministry of Earth Sciences has implemented various measures to strengthen disaster early warning systems for cyclones, heavy rainfall, and other extreme weather events across the country, including in Maharashtra. These measures are applicable across all seasons, including the ongoing southwest monsoon. The major initiatives are as follows:

  • Augmentation of the observational network.
  • Development of indigenous, technology-driven, and citizen-centric weather forecasting systems that strengthen disaster preparedness and improve public safety across India. IMD's in-house developed Decision Support System (DSS) is a major step in the direction of promoting self-reliance under the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative. As a result, there is 40% improvement in forecast accuracy for all types of severe weather events in recent decades as compared to the previous decade.
  • Impact-based forecasts and risk-based warnings are being disseminated at the district level, empowering authorities to take timely preventive actions against cyclones, heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, heatwaves, and cold waves.
  • Developed "Mausamgram" (Har Har Mausam, Har Ghar Mausam), a unique citizen-focused platform providing location-specific, hyperlocal weather forecasts down to the village level. "Mausamgram" delivers hourly forecasts for the next 36 hours, three-hourly forecasts for the next five days, and six-hourly forecasts for up to ten days. Users can conveniently access weather information by searching through PIN code or location name, or by selecting the state, district, block, and gram panchayat. This user-friendly system ensures easy access to hyperlocal forecasts, enabling citizens to obtain accurate and timely weather updates tailored to their specific location.
  • Development of climate hazard and vulnerability maps at the district level (https://imdpune.gov.in/hazardatlas/index.html)
  • Development of geospatial services for weather forecast and warnings (https://imdgeospatial.imd.gov.in/)
  • IMD is one of the agencies that generates Common Alert Protocol (CAP) alerts for severe weather warnings. These CAP alerts are disseminated through SMS as well as the SACHET app, developed by the NDMA. These CAP feeds are also being used by APPLE, GOOGLE, and GMAS for the dissemination of weather-related warnings. IMD has developed an Application Programming Interface (API), which is being used by various private and public organisations for further dissemination of IMD's forecasts and warnings to the general public through different media, including mobile apps developed by different stakeholders.
  • IMD has developed various mobile apps for the dissemination of weather-related warnings, such as the MAUSAM App for weather forecasting and warnings, MEGHDOOT App for agro met services, DAMINI App for lightning warnings, and UMANG App for Weather forecasting and warnings.

            To enhance the local relevance and last-mile dissemination of weather information in remote and vulnerable regions, the India Meteorological Department, in coordination with other Ministries and stakeholders, has implemented the following major initiatives to support disaster preparedness during cyclones, heavy rainfall, and other extreme weather events. These initiatives are applicable across all seasons, including the ongoing southwest monsoon.

  • In collaboration with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, IMD has developed the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, providing Panchayat-level weather forecasts through e-GramSwaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), Meri Panchayat App, e-Manchitra, and Mausamgram (https://mausamgram.imd.gov.in).
  • The mobile numbers of Panchayat Members, Ward Members, and Panchayat Secretaries have been integrated with the Panchayat Mausam Seva Portal, enabling the timely dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories through WhatsApp for further dissemination at the Gram Panchayat level.
  • IMD also leverages the Krishi Sakhis and Pashu Sakhis network of the Ministry of Rural Development for last-mile dissemination of weather forecasts and agrometeorological advisories.
  • IMD has organized over 7,300 Farmers' Awareness Programs (FAPs) across 373 districts, benefiting nearly 3.67 lakh farmers, including 83 Aspirational Districts, to promote climate-resilient agriculture and the effective use of weather-based advisory services.
  • Under Mission Mausam, IMD has developed KALP (Krishi Advisory based on Location-specific Weather Prediction) for the generation of location-, crop- and crop-stage-specific advisories and Mausam SANKALP (Systematic Agrometeorological aNalytics, Knowledge and Advisory enabLing Platform) to strengthen weather analytics, advisory generation and climate-resilient agricultural planning.
  • Timely alerts are transmitted in real-time to the Ministry of Home Affairs, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs), District Magistrates, health departments, and public utility sectors.
  • A direct, real-time coordination mechanism is maintained with District Collectors, SDMAs, the Department of Agriculture, and other local stakeholders to ensure rapid ground-level dissemination and administrative preparedness.

2288187.title: Indian Railways Approves ₹440 Crore Third Line Project Between Nimpura West Outer Cabin and Midnapur of South Eastern Railway
2288187.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Approves ₹440 Crore Third Line Project Between Nimpura West Outer Cabin and Midnapur of South Eastern Railway
14.52 km Third Line to Enhance Passenger & Freight Movement on High Utilisation Network Route
Project to Support Additional 3.52 MTPA Traffic and Strengthen Movement of Coal, Iron Ore, Steel, Cement and Other Essential Commodities
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 12:05PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards enhancing rail capacity on one of the country's important freight corridors, Indian Railways has approved the construction of a 14.52 km third line between Nimpura West Outer Cabin and Midnapur in South Eastern Railway at a cost of ₹440 crore.

The project forms part of Indian Railways' continued efforts to augment network capacity on high-density routes to facilitate faster movement of passenger and freight trains while supporting the growing transportation needs of industries and essential commodities.

Third Line Between Nimpura West Outer Cabin and Midnapur

The sanctioned project involves construction of a 14.52 km third line between Nimpura West Outer Cabin and Midnapur on South Eastern Railway.

The section forms part of the High Utilisation Network (HUN-2) route, where the Nimpura West Outer Cabin-Gokulpur section is presently a single line, while doubling works are already in progress. The additional third line will substantially augment line capacity and improve operational flexibility on this strategically important corridor.

Boost to Freight Capacity and Passenger Operations

The route carries substantial volumes of passenger as well as freight traffic transporting key commodities including manganese, iron ore, containers, coal, clinker, pellet iron, iron and steel, wheat, stone, sleepers, slag, salt, rice, petroleum products, limestone, gypsum, fertilisers, edible oil, chemical salt, charcoal, cement, ballast and ash, with an overall freight loading of nearly 23.80 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA).

The existing section is operating at a line capacity utilisation of 115.71%, indicating severe congestion. The third line will create additional capacity to accommodate growing passenger and freight traffic while improving operational efficiency across the corridor.

Supporting Economic Growth Through Higher Rail Capacity

Upon completion, the project is expected to facilitate additional freight traffic of 3.52 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA). The enhanced infrastructure will improve movement of essential commodities, reduce operational bottlenecks, increase network reliability and strengthen connectivity for industries and businesses dependent on this important rail corridor.

The approval reflects Indian Railways' sustained focus on capacity augmentation across high-density routes, enabling faster movement of freight and passengers while supporting economic growth through a modern, efficient and future-ready railway network.

 *****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma

Vice-President Pays Floral Tributes to Freedom Fighter Thiru Subramania Siva on His Death Anniversary
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 11:18AM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today paid floral tributes to the great freedom fighter Thiru Subramania Siva at the Uprashtrapati Bhawan on the occasion of his death anniversary.

Speaking on the occasion, the Vice-President said:

“The great freedom fighter Thiru Subramania Siva hailed from the small town of Vatlagundu in the southern part of Tamil Nadu. He travelled to every village, inspiring people to dedicate themselves to India’s freedom with the vibrant slogan ‘Vande Mataram’. Along with the legendary freedom fighter Thiru V. O. Chidambaram Pillai, he was imprisoned by the British colonial government for his unwavering commitment to the nation’s freedom.

Despite contracting leprosy during his imprisonment, he never allowed it to weaken his resolve and continued to serve the cause of India’s independence until his last breath. A deeply patriotic son of India, he worshipped Bharat Mata as his God and devoted his entire life to the service of the motherland.

On his death anniversary, the nation pays its deepest respects and heartfelt tributes to this great patriot."

2288143.title: 36th Basic Course in Legislative Drafting Inaugurated to Strengthen Uniform and Effective Law-Making Across India
2288143.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
36th Basic Course in Legislative Drafting Inaugurated to Strengthen Uniform and Effective Law-Making Across India
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 10:29AM by PIB Delhi

The 36th Basic Course in Legislative Drafting, organised by the Institute of Legislative Drafting and Research (ILDR), Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, was inaugurated on 22 July, 2026 at Vidhayi Sabhagar, Kartavya Bhavan-02, New Delhi, for officers of the State Governments and Union territories. The inaugural session was graced by the presence of Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department & Department of Legal Affairs, Dr. Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary and Course Director (ILDR), and other senior officers of the Department.

On the occasion, Dr. Rajiv Mani emphasized the need for uniform legislative drafting across the country to ensure clarity, consistency and legal certainty in laws, particularly in the era of grassroots legislative reforms, thereby facilitating their effective implementation.

The inauguration of the Course reaffirms the Legislative Department's long-standing commitment to strengthening legislative drafting capacity across the country through structured training and capacity-building initiatives.

The said Course, being conducted from 22nd July, 2026 to 25th September, 2026, has brought together 18 trainee officers from thirteen State Governments and one Union territory. It aims to enhance the participants' understanding of the principles of legislative drafting while providing practical exposure to the drafting of legislative instruments, thereby equipping them with the knowledge and skills required for effective legislative drafting.

The programme is expected to further promote uniformity, precision and excellence in legislative drafting and strengthen the institutional capacity of State Governments and Union territories.

2288139.title: Four CSIR Technologies Licensed to Industry and Smart Rural Water Monitoring Technology Commercially Launched
2288139.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Four CSIR Technologies Licensed to Industry and Smart Rural Water Monitoring Technology Commercially Launched
Posted On: 23 JUL 2026 10:04AM by PIB Delhi

The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) today organized a Technology Transfer Event at the CSIR Headquarters, New Delhi, bringing together scientists, industry partners, technology adopters and strategic stakeholders. The programme, organized by CSIR-Central Scientific Instruments Organisation (CSIR-CSIO), Chandigarh, witnessed the transfer of four indigenous technologies to industry, the commercial launch of an IoT-enabled rural water service delivery, measurement and monitoring system, and recognition of royalty received from Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Panchkula, for licensed production of indigenous defence technologies.

The event was graced by Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR & Secretary, DSIR, and attended by senior officials, scientists and staff members from CSIR Headquarters, CSIR-CSIO and industry partners.

Presenting an overview of the technology transfers and royalty achievements, Prof. Shantanu Bhattacharya, Director, CSIR-CSIO, highlighted the laboratory's growing innovation and technology commercialization ecosystem. He outlined the technologies transferred to industry, including the Induction Motor Stethoscope (MSCOPE), Portable & Universal Motor-cum-Pump Performance Monitor (PU-MPPM) and i-Power Quality Analyser (IPQA), which were licensed to M/s Pump Academy Private Limited, Bengaluru. The Optical Module and Beam Combiner Assembly for Head-Up Display (HUD) for SU-30 aircraft programmes was transferred to Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Panchkula. He also announced the commercial launch of the Affordable IoT-enabled Water Service Delivery, Measurement and Monitoring Sensing System for Rural Deployment through M/s Biometry Technologies Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi, enabling advanced monitoring of water quality, quantity and service delivery in rural areas.

Prof. Bhattacharya further highlighted that CSIR-CSIO has consistently strengthened its technology commercialization initiatives and informed the gathering that the laboratory received ₹1.67 crore as royalty from BEL, Panchkula during FY 2025-26 for licensed production of indigenous military avionics technologies, including Head-Up Display (HUD), Drogue Lights, Taxi Landing Lights, HUD I Level Tester and Boresight Alignment Tool technologies. He noted that the achievement reflects CSIR-CSIO's sustained partnership with Indian industry and its growing contribution to indigenous defence manufacturing.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR & Secretary, DSIR, congratulated the CSIR-CSIO team on the successful technology transfers and commercialization initiatives. She appreciated the efforts of the laboratory under the leadership of Prof. Shantanu Bhattacharya in accelerating technology development, increasing external cash flow (ECF), expanding industry partnerships and enhancing technology transfer. She emphasized that successful commercialization of indigenous technologies is central to CSIR's mission of translating research into products and processes that create value for industry while delivering tangible benefits to society. The DG, CSIR encouraged scientists across the CSIR network to continue pursuing impactful, industry-oriented research aligned with national priorities and the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat.

The event concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Head, Business Development Group (BDG), CSIR-CSIO.

Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of 100% of the equity share capital of NCR Atleos Corporation (Target) by The Brink's Company (Acquirer)
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 8:57PM by PIB Delhi

Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of 100% of the equity share capital of NCR Atleos Corporation (Target) by The Brink's Company (Acquirer).

The Proposed Combination entails the acquisition of 100% of the equity share capital of the Target by the Acquirer. Post completion, the Target shall be wholly owned and controlled by the Acquirer.

The Acquirer is a global provider of cash and valuables management, digital retail solutions and ATM managed services, operating in over 100 countries. In India, the Acquirer principally provides cash replenishment services and ancillary first-line maintenance service through its subsidiary Brink's India Private Limited.

The Target is a financial technology company providing self-directed banking solutions globally. In India, the Target's activities principally comprise: (i) manufacture and supply of ATM hardware, including through its Chennai manufacturing facility; (ii) development and licensing of ATM software; (iii) ATM managed services, including monitoring, help-desk and transaction processing; and (iv) ATM maintenance services, i.e., first-line maintenance  and second line maintenance.

Detailed order of the Commission will follow.

2288053.title: Ministry of Coal Releases 'AAROH': India's First Report on Scientific Mine Closure and Repurposing Practices
2288053.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal Releases 'AAROH': India's First Report on Scientific Mine Closure and Repurposing Practices
Ministry of Coal also Signs Implementation Agreement with Germany's GIZ to Boost Scientific Mine Closure Cooperation
Coal Minister Inaugurates Coal NEER Plants, Turning Mine Discharge into Safe Drinking Water
BCCL, JRDA Sign Tripartite MoUs with Hindalco and Rajdhani Universal Fabrics for Jharia Rehabilitation and Skill Development
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal today released ‘AAROH: Annual Report on Mine Closure’ at the Oberoi, New Delhi, highlighting India’s progress in adopting scientific approaches to mine closure, ecological restoration, and sustainable post-mining land utilisation.

The event was graced by Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal and Mines; Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and Minister of State for the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space; Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines; H.E. Dr Philipp Ackermann, German Ambassador;  Dr. Ewa Suwara, Deputy Head of the EU Delegation;  Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal; Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal and Shri Sajeesh Kumar N., Coal Controller. The program witnessed participation from other senior officials of Central and State Governments, coal companies, international organisations, industry, academia, and other stakeholders associated with sustainable mining and post-mining development.

The Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G Kishan Reddy inaugurated the Exhibition on Mine Closure and Mine Repurposing, showcasing innovative initiatives undertaken by Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries, NLC India Limited, Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL), NTPC and private mining organisations. The exhibition highlighted successful practices in scientific reclamation, ecological restoration, mine repurposing, community development, and sustainable utilisation of post-mining land.

The Ministers formally released ‘AAROH – Annual Report on Mine Closure’, followed by the screening of a documentary film showcasing the publication. The AAROH, developed by the Coal Controller Organisation, presents India’s first comprehensive documentation of scientific mine closure and repurposing practices. The report documents the transformative journey of 42 scientifically closed coal mines, showcasing structured reclamation processes, ecological restoration initiatives, sustainable post-mining land utilisation, and community-oriented interventions that have contributed to the creation of environmentally restored and socially beneficial landscapes.

Each mine profile featured in AAROH presents key closure initiatives, post-mining land-use outcomes, before-and-after visual documentation, and QR code-enabled documentary videos capturing the transformation journey of the respective mine sites. The publication serves as a knowledge repository, highlighting successful models and providing valuable insights for future mine closure and repurposing efforts.

The report also captures the evolution of India’s mine closure framework and highlights key initiatives of the Ministry of Coal, including the RECLAIM Framework, L.I.V.E.S. Framework, SUVIKALP – Mine Repurposing Tool, and SUVIKALP Samvaad, which promote scientific assessment, stakeholder participation, knowledge exchange, and sustainable post-mining land use.

Another highlight of the event was the signing of the Implementation Agreement between the Ministry of Coal and Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) for technical cooperation on ‘To-be closed mines’. The agreement aims to strengthen collaboration in scientific mine closure, mine repurposing, technical capacity building, knowledge exchange, and adoption of global best practices, further strengthening India-Germany cooperation in the mining sector. The project has been commissioned by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and is co-financed by the European Union, with a total project volume of EUR 10 million until 2030. The cooperation will take place over the next four years focusing on developing innovative and sustainable approaches for the closure and repurposing of coal mines in India. This investment by Germany and the European Union reflects Team Europe’s strong partnership with India to deepen cooperation on sustainable economic development, a priority reaffirmed at the 16th India–EU Summit and the visit of German Chancellor to India earlier this year.

The Union Minister also virtually inaugurated Coal NEER Plants established by Coal India Limited through its subsidiaries—Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL), Central Coalfields Limited (CCL), Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), and South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL). The initiative is aimed at strengthening access to safe and sustainable drinking water facilities in coal-bearing regions and improving the quality of life of communities residing in mining areas. Aligning with the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Waste to Wealth’, these plants purify mine water and markets it as safe, high-quality bottled drinking water under the brand name ‘Coal Neer.’ These projects use advanced treatment methods including RO, UV and CDI technologies to provide safe, clean, and affordable drinking water to nearby villages and local communities. Apart from providing affordable bottled drinking water, these projects also offer sustainable livelihood opportunities for Self Help Groups from nearby villages.

The event also witnessed the signing of tripartite Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) by Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) and Jharia Rehabilitation and Development Authority (JRDA) with Hindalco Industries Limited and Rajdhani Universal Fabrics Private Limited. These partnerships will facilitate coordinated efforts towards rehabilitation, infrastructure development, community welfare, and socio-economic development in the Jharia coalfield region. The MoU signed between BCCL, JRDA and Hindalco aims to establish an Industry-Linked Skill Centre that will equip the youth of the Dhanbad region with industry-relevant skills to work in world-class apparel manufacturing units. The MoU signed between BCCL, JRDA and Rajdhani Universal Fabrics Pvt Ltd aims to establish a world-class integrated technical textile manufacturing ecosystem, which will generate large-scale employment and strengthen skill development.

In his keynote address, Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G Kishan Reddy, mentioned that under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has fundamentally transformed the philosophy of mine closure, viewing it not as the end of mining but as the beginning of new opportunities for people, communities and sustainable development. He described scientific mine closure as a national priority and a key pillar of the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, adding that India has scientifically closed 42 coal mines, including 33 in the last year alone, and has set an ambitious target of scientifically closing 147 more mines over the next two to three years. He highlighted that the Ministry has built a comprehensive ecosystem for mine closure through the RECLAIM Framework, the SUVIKALP digital platform, the A.R.T.H.A. Framework, and District Collector-led Mine Closure Advisory Committees, while the Mine Closure Guidelines, 2025 place people and sustainability at the heart of mine closure. The Minister further informed that, for the first time, 25 per cent of the approved mine closure cost has been earmarked for community development, creating an investment potential of nearly ₹10,000 crore over the next decade. He also announced that the Government has created a dedicated corpus of over USD 5 billion (approximately ₹40,000 crore) for scientific mine closure and progressive mine closure, demonstrating its long-term commitment to environmentally responsible mining, ecological restoration and the socio-economic development of mining-affected regions.

Highlighting the transformative potential of scientific mine closure, the Minister said reclaimed mine lands across the country are being repurposed for renewable energy, eco-tourism, water conservation, agriculture, community infrastructure and sustainable livelihood generation, citing successful examples from West Bokaro, Bishrampur and the Viveknagar Solar Project. Referring to global best practices, particularly Germany's experience in mine closure and Just Transition, he said the implementation agreement between the Ministry of Coal and GIZ would combine Germany's expertise with India's scale, policy leadership and implementation capacity to create an Indian model of mine closure that integrates environmental protection, technological innovation, community participation and economic opportunity. Emphasising that successful mine closure requires the collective efforts of governments, industry, academia, civil society, local communities and international partners, he expressed confidence that together they would transform every closed mine into a source of hope, opportunity and prosperity for future generations.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, remarked that "the time has come to change the phrase from mine closure to mine of wealth." He lauded the Ministry of Coal for its progressive policies on scientific mine closure, stating that the successful closure of 42 coal mines demonstrates how degraded mine lands can be transformed into productive assets through ecological restoration, afforestation, water conservation, renewable energy and other sustainable community-centric initiatives. He noted that these efforts embody the principles of the circular economy by turning waste into wealth. Appreciating the India–Germany partnership and increasing private sector participation in scientific mine closure, he reaffirmed India's commitment to achieving its Net Zero target by 2070.

In his address, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State for Coal and Mines, emphasised that the Ministry of Coal is committed to ensuring that the benefits of mining extend far beyond coal production and translate into meaningful improvements in the lives of people living in coal-bearing regions. He said the Ministry's approach to scientific mine closure is guided by the principle that environmental restoration and socio-economic development must progress together. Referring to the Indo-German technical cooperation initiative, he said the partnership will strengthen institutional capacities, facilitate the exchange of global expertise and support the adoption of best practices in scientific mine closure and sustainable post-mining development, enabling closed mines to be transformed into assets that promote ecological restoration, sustainable livelihoods and long-term regional development.

Highlighting the significance of Coal NEER and the Tripartite MoUs under the Jharia Master Plan, Shri Dubey said these initiatives reflect the Ministry's commitment to translating sustainable mining practices into tangible community benefits. While Coal NEER will improve access to safe drinking water, promote efficient water resource management and generate livelihood opportunities through the active participation of local Self-Help Groups, particularly women, the Jharia initiative will complement rehabilitation with industry-linked skill development and employment opportunities, ensuring long-term socio-economic empowerment for rehabilitated families.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, emphasised that mining must be guided by conscience, with people and their lives at the centre of development in mining regions. He described mine closure as a critical stage in the life cycle of mining, where responsible resource extraction must transition into long-term environmental restoration, land repurposing and sustainable community development. He noted that the Ministry of Coal has transformed mine closure from a regulatory requirement into a planned, people-centric process through the Mine Closure Guidelines, 2025, comprehensive frameworks and digital tools developed by the Coal Controller Organisation, ensuring that environmental rehabilitation, community participation and future land use are integrated into every stage of mine closure planning. Referring to the signing of the Implementation Agreement for the Indo-German Technical Cooperation Project on "To-be-Closed Coal Mines" under the Indo-German Green and Sustainable Development Partnership, he said the EUR 10 million grant from the Government of Germany and the European Union would enable India to adopt global best practices in scientific mine closure while reinforcing the shared vision that mine closure is not merely the end of mining, but the beginning of new opportunities for people, communities and the environment.

Highlighting the Ministry's commitment to inclusive post-mining development, the Secretary said that the Revised Jharia Master Plan goes beyond rehabilitation by creating sustainable livelihood opportunities through skill development and the establishment of a Plug-and-Play Textile Manufacturing Facility for rehabilitated families. He also highlighted the significant contribution of coal PSUs in supplying nearly 300 lakh kiloliters of treated mine water annually, benefiting around three lakh people, including the supply of drinking water to Chennai. Referring to the launch of Coal NEER, he said the initiative demonstrates how treated mine discharge water can be transformed into safe drinking water for nearby communities, exemplifying the Ministry's commitment to scientific innovation, sustainable resource management and community welfare.

Addressing the gathering, H.E. Dr. Philipp Ackermann, Ambassador of Germany to India and Bhutan, highlighted the continuing India–Germany partnership in advancing sustainable development. Referring to the Implementation Agreement between the Ministry of Coal and GIZ, he said the collaboration would facilitate the exchange of technical expertise and global best practices for scientific mine closure and sustainable mine repurposing, while further strengthening Indo-German cooperation for a just and sustainable transition in mining regions.

In her address, Dr. Ewa Suwara, Deputy Head of the EU Delegation to India said that the partnership between India and EU is founded on shared democratic values, mutual respect and a common commitment sustainable development. She said the Government of India’s commitment to sustainable closure of abandoned mines reflects a forward looking and responsible approach. She added that successful closure of mines requires long term planning, active engagement with stakeholders, investment in skill and reskill, land restoration and a firm commitment to ensure that the transition is fair and inclusive. She said that in this context, today’s implementation agreement represents a significant and practical step forward. She also said that the agreement gives concrete expression to the shared ambition and lays the foundation for tangible cooperation through technical assistance and capacity building.

The event reaffirmed the Ministry of Coal’s commitment to advancing scientific mine closure through progressive policies, technological innovation, institutional partnerships, and community-focused initiatives. Through initiatives such as AAROH, the Ministry continues to strengthen India’s framework for responsible mining, ecological restoration, and sustainable post-mining development, contributing towards the vision of Viksit Bharat.

****

2288042.title: India, Panama Chart New Maritime Partnership Focused on Logistics, Digital Innovation and Global Connectivity
2288042.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2288042.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
India, Panama Chart New Maritime Partnership Focused on Logistics, Digital Innovation and Global Connectivity
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi
  • India & Panama identify Maritime Security, Logistics, Skilling and Digital Transformation as key pillars of bilateral cooperation
  • Panama as a strategic gateway to Latin America, India seeks deeper collaboration in shipping, ports and maritime infrastructure

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways  (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal held bilateral talks with Panama's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Javier Martínez-Acha Vásquez, to deepen maritime cooperation between the two countries, with both sides identifying logistics, shipping, maritime security, skill development and digital transformation as the key pillars of an expanded strategic partnership.

"India and Panama are natural maritime partners. By combining Panama's strategic logistics strengths with India's growing maritime capabilities, we can build resilient supply chains, strengthen global connectivity and create new opportunities for trade, investment, innovation and sustainable growth. Our shared vision is to transform this partnership into one of the key pillars of India's engagement with Latin America and the Caribbean," said Sarbananda Sonowal, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

The discussions reaffirmed the long-standing maritime relationship between India and Panama, dating back to the 19th century, and recognised the significant contribution of the Indian diaspora in strengthening bilateral ties. With India emerging as a global ports leader and Panama serving as one of the world's foremost maritime logistics hubs, both countries agreed that closer collaboration and the exchange of best practices would unlock new opportunities for trade, connectivity and investment across the Americas.

During the meeting, Minister Javier Martínez-Acha Vásquez outlined four priority areas for expanding maritime cooperation between the two countries, maritime security, technical collaboration between India's Directorate General of Shipping and the Panama Maritime Authority, maritime education and skilling, and future-oriented cooperation in digital maritime transformation, including artificial intelligence, smart port logistics and maritime single-window systems.

Minister Sonowal highlighted India's rapid transformation under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi through sustained investments in ports, shipping, inland waterways, logistics, shipbuilding, cruise tourism and green maritime initiatives. He reiterated that Panama is India's natural gateway to Central America, Latin America and the Caribbean, and stressed the need to improve shipping connectivity, deepen logistics partnerships and accelerate institutional cooperation to realise the untapped potential of bilateral trade.

"Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India's maritime sector is undergoing a transformational journey driven by world-class infrastructure, modern logistics, green shipping and digital innovation. Our vision is not merely to build ports, but to build partnerships that connect economies and create shared prosperity. Panama, with its strategic maritime strengths, is a natural partner in this journey, and together we can shape a more resilient, efficient and future-ready global maritime ecosystem," said Sarbananda Sonowal.

Sonowal also proposed expediting discussions on a bilateral agreement on maritime transportation and port development, expanding cooperation in green ship recycling, strengthening seafarer welfare and skill development, and promoting collaboration in port modernisation, warehousing, digital innovation and maritime infrastructure. Minister Sonowal invited Panama's Minister of Maritime Affairs to participate in India Maritime Week 2026 in New Delhi as both sides agreed to carry forward discussions through stronger institutional partnerships.

2288009.title: DRDO inks two major contracts with Industry partners as part of AEW&C MK-II programme
2288009.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
DRDO inks two major contracts with Industry partners as part of AEW&C MK-II programme
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 8:19PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant boost to Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Centre for Air Borne Systems (CABS), DRDO has signed a contract with AI Engineering Services Limited (AIESL), New Delhi for the conversion of six A321 Aircraft from commercial to green configuration, further leading to the development and production of Airborne Early Warning & Control (AEW&C) MKII Programme. A separate contract was inked with Adani Defence Systems and Technologies (ADSTL), Ahmedabad to engage with the company as Development Cum Production Partner (DcPP) for Mission Systems designed for the AEW&C MKII Programme.

The contracts were signed by Director CABS with CEO, AIESL and Head-Airborne Platform, ADSTL in the presence of Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi on July 22, 2026.

CABS, DRDO with support from ADSTL as DcPP is responsible for integration of mission systems on modified AEW&C MK II Platform, delivered by Airbus Defence & Space (Original Equipment Manufacturer). CABS and ADSTL will also carry out flight testing of the AEW&C MK II aircraft along with the Indian Air Force to obtain certification from airworthiness agencies - Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification and Directorate General of Aeronautical Quality Assurance.

AEW&C Mk II System from DRDO with CABS as the nodal laboratory will provide enhanced endurance, advanced airborne surveillance, secure communication, improved situational awareness and enhanced command and control capabilities. This, in turn, will give a significant boost to the air defence capabilities and aid in neutralising threats across extended ranges.

The engagement of industries reaffirms the commitment of the Government to achieve self-reliance for fostering a robust ecosystem towards innovation, research and manufacturing within the country.

2287985.title: NBA releases Rs 6.67 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing Mechanism for Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Support in 11 cotton-growing States
2287985.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2287985.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
NBA releases Rs 6.67 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing Mechanism for Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Support in 11 cotton-growing States
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has released Rs 6.67 crore under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism to support biodiversity conservation, sustainable utilisation of biological resources and livelihood enhancement in 11 cotton-growing States. The disbursement demonstrates how benefits derived from the commercial utilisation of biological resources are being reinvested in biodiversity conservation and community welfare under the Biological Diversity Act.

The benefit-sharing amount of Rs 7.62 crore has been realised from M/s Bayer Science & Innovation Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Monsanto Holdings Pvt. Ltd.) for research involving 25,431 cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) varieties. Cotton occupies a unique place in India's agricultural and economic landscape, with the country serving as a global reservoir of cotton genetic diversity that supports nearly 4-5 crore people across the value chain. Since the biological resources were accessed through traders and intermediaries, identifying individual conservers or benefit claimers was not feasible.

To address such situations, the NBA, with the support of an Expert Committee, has developed transparent modalities for the utilisation of ABS amounts. Where the geographical occurrence of a biological resource can be reliably established using published records, the corresponding ABS amount is allocated to the concerned State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) for biodiversity conservation, sustainable utilisation and socio-economic development of the concerned areas. Where the source cannot be established, the funds are retained in the National Biodiversity Fund and utilised in accordance with Section 27 of the Biological Diversity Act for conservation and sustainable use of biological resources across the country.

Applying these modalities, the NBA has allocated Rs 6.67 among eleven cotton-growing States: Maharashtra (Rs 2.41 crore), Gujarat (Rs 1.38 crore), Telangana (Rs 1.06 crore), Karnataka (Rs 0.40 crore), Rajasthan (Rs 0.36 crore), Madhya Pradesh (Rs 0.31 crore), Andhra Pradesh (Rs 0.23 crore), Haryana (Rs 0.23 crore), Odisha (Rs 0.14 crore), Punjab (Rs 0.09 crore) and Tamil Nadu (Rs 0.06 crore). The remaining amount (Rs 0.95 crore) has been earmarked for the NBA as per the Biological Diversity Rules. 

The allocation is based on the geographical distribution of cotton cultivation using data from the All India Coordinated Research Project on Cotton (AICRP), ICAR, and is proportional to each State's area under cotton cultivation, ensuring a transparent, scientific and equitable distribution of ABS benefits.

The allocation will support on-farm and ex-situ conservation of biological resources, documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, ecosystem restoration, strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites, documentation of traditional knowledge, biodiversity research, development of digital biodiversity databases, capacity building of Biodiversity Management Committees, awareness programmes and livelihood enhancement. These investments will help conserve valuable genetic traits for future crop improvement while empowering local communities as custodians of India's agrobiodiversity.

The initiative also establishes a transparent and science-based model for distributing ABS benefits where biological resources are sourced through complex supply chains. By linking benefit-sharing to the verified geographical occurrence of biological resources, it ensures that ABS reaches biodiversity-rich regions even when individual beneficiaries cannot be identified.

With this disbursement, the total ABS funds released by the NBA have reached Rs 152.24 crore. The initiative demonstrates how the ABS mechanism transforms the commercial utilisation of biological resources to combine economy, ecology and equity. It also contributes to the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, particularly Target 13 on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources, while supporting Target 4 on conserving genetic diversity.

The National Biodiversity Authority is a statutory body established under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, functioning under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol's principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits.

2287997.title: Centre and States are equal partners in building a future-ready education system for Viksit Bharat 2047 – Shri Dharmendra Pradhan
2287997.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Centre and States are equal partners in building a future-ready education system for Viksit Bharat 2047 – Shri Dharmendra Pradhan
Our collective success will be measured by the learning outcomes we achieve and the opportunities we create for every child – Union Minister for Education
Shri Dharmendra Pradhan, chairs the two-day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers to review Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of School Education and Literacy
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 8:02PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Education, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan today said that the Centre and the States are equal partners in strengthening school education. He was chairing the two-day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers to review Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Ministry of Education, at the ICAR National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi.

In his address, Shri Pradhan emphasised that the Conclave provides a valuable platform for the Centre and the States and UTs to strengthen cooperation, share best practices, and accelerate the effective implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes in line with the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. He said the deliberations would further reinforce the collective commitment towards building a future-ready, inclusive and high-quality school education system and contribute to the upcoming PRAGATI review chaired by the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi.

Shri Pradhan highlighted the progress made in school education through initiatives such as Samagra Shiksha, PM SHRI, NIPUN Bharat, PM POSHAN and ULLAS, and called upon the States and UTs to continue working together to strengthen foundational literacy and numeracy, empower teachers, leverage technology and AI, promote innovation, and ensure the holistic development of every learner towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The Minister urged the states to promote the mother tongue of the child and multilingualism to strengthen foundational learning and improve learning outcomes.

Addressing the Conclave, Minister of State for Education and Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Shri Jayant Chaudhary, emphasised on the importance of collaborative efforts between the Centre and States and UTs to strengthen school education and improve educational outcomes.

 

The Conclave aims to advance the shared vision of an equitable, inclusive and quality school education system, contributing to the realisation of the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The sessions focussed on strengthening the implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes and improving educational outcomes. Education Ministers of States and UTs reaffirmed the importance of Centre–State collaboration, knowledge sharing and the shared commitment to ensuring equitable, inclusive and quality education for every learner.

The first day featured presentations by Additional Secretary, DoSEL, Shri Dheeraj Sahu, on Samagra Shiksha and issues for consideration under the PRAGATI framework, and Deputy Director General, DoSEL, Dr. Pankaj K. P. Shreyaskar, on the status of educational indicators in States and UTs. Joint Secretary, DoSEL, Dr. Amarpreet Duggal, and  Economic Advisor, DoSEL ,Ms. A. Srija also participated in the proceedings along with senior officials from the Union Ministry of Education and the States.

2287971.title: Government Promotes Re-Employment Opportunities For Senior Citizens Through National Career Service (NCS) Portal
2287971.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Promotes Re-Employment Opportunities For Senior Citizens Through National Career Service (NCS) Portal
Population Of Persons Aged 60 Years And Above Expected To Increase To 20.8 Per Cent By 2050, To Further Reach 36 Per Cent By The End Of The Century: Union Minister For Social Justice And Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar
NCS Portal Hosts 1.68 Lakh Suitable Vacancies For Senior Citizen Candidates, 1.89 Lakh Senior Citizen Job Seekers Registered On NCS Portal
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has reaffirmed its commitment to promote active ageing and enhancing employment opportunities for senior citizens through the National Career Service (NCS) Portal. The dedicated Senior Citizen Re-employment Initiative has witnessed significant growth in registrations, employer participation and job opportunities, enabling experienced professionals to continue contributing to the nation's workforce.

This information was given by Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar in Rajya Sabha while replying to the question by Member of the House Shri Rajinder Gupta.

The Minister informed the House that the Government has taken note of the findings of the UNFPA-India's India Ageing Report 2023, which projects a significant rise in the country's elderly population. He said the report suggests that the population of persons aged 60 years and above is expected to increase from 10.4 per cent in 2022 to 20.8 per cent by 2050, and further reach 36 per cent by the end of the century.

Dr Kumar added that the report also highlights the need for policies that ensure livelihood opportunities and structured re-employment avenues to provide income security for elderly persons, particularly those working in the unorganised sector.

The Minister further informed that under the NCS project, the Government has approved 407 Model Career Centres (MCCs) in collaboration with States and institutions. These centres connect youth and other job seekers, including senior citizens with employment opportunities through job fairs, the NCS Portal, career counselling and training.

Dr Kumar stated that the National Career Service is playing a pivotal role in supporting India's vision of a skilled, employable and future-ready workforce adding that the platform evolving through AI-driven services, greater convergence and enhanced citizen-centric offerings, is expected to strengthen the country's modern employment services framework and contribute to inclusive economic growth and employment generation.

The Minister said that since the inception of the NCS Portal in 2015, more than 6.46 crore job seekers and 58.76 lakh employers have registered on the portal, including 1.89 lakh job seekers above the age of 60 years.

Pertinently, the portal currently hosts 1.68 lakh vacancies identified as suitable for candidates above the age of 60 years. In addition, more than 2.29 crore job seekers, including senior citizens, have been shortlisted by employers through the portal across the country.

2287957.title: PM Chairs High-Level Meeting of Secretaries to Review Progress of Rural Development, Agriculture, Social Welfare and Allied Sectors towards Viksit Bharat Goals
2287957.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM Chairs High-Level Meeting of Secretaries to Review Progress of Rural Development, Agriculture, Social Welfare and Allied Sectors towards Viksit Bharat Goals
PM emphasises that the welfare of citizens must remain at the heart of all reforms
PM Stresses the Need to Evolve Governance Processes in Line with Changing Times
PM Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach and breaking silos to achieve the nation's development goals
PM says that dream to build a Viksit Bharat should become a Jan Andolan and Youth should be it’s foundation
PM underscores the Need for Coordinated Action to Combat Drug Abuse and Empower Youth
PM Stresses Integrated Approach to Position India as a Global Sports Hub
PM Highlights Transformative Potential of PM-KUSUM and Need for Global Skill Mapping
Secretaries share their experiences and perspectives on various initiatives and challenges in their respective domains
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister today chaired a high-level meeting with Secretaries to review progress of rural development, agriculture, social welfare and allied sectors towards Viksit Bharat Goals, at his residence at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg earlier today.

Prime Minister emphasised that the welfare of citizens must remain at the heart of all reforms. He said that reforms designed around people's needs should gather real momentum and deliver meaningful transformation. He emphasised that the objective of reforms is not merely to improve the functioning of the Government, but to accelerate India's journey towards becoming a developed nation.

Prime Minister highlighted that governance systems are witnessing rapid changes and stressed the importance of adapting and strengthening governance processes to effectively meet the needs of a dynamic and evolving environment. He suggested undertaking a comprehensive mapping of emerging requirements across various Ministries and Departments.

Prime Minister stressed the need for a whole-of-government approach to achieve the nation's development goals. He further emphasised that the dream to build a Viksit Bharat should become a Jan Andolan and that India's youth should form the foundation of this vision.

Prime Minister underscored the importance of tackling the serious issue of drug abuse among youth. He suggested that efforts should be made to develop an institutional mechanism to break departmental silos and foster greater inter-departmental coordination and convergence in youth-centric initiatives.

Prime Minister further emphasized the need to adopt an integrated approach for the development of sports. He noted that, with sports tourism emerging as a key focus area, India should aspire to host major international sporting events to establish itself as a global sports hub. He stressed the importance of promoting technology and fostering innovation through startups in the sports sector.

Prime Minister highlighted that the widespread adoption of initiatives such as the PM KUSUM Scheme by farmers can bring transformative changes to the agriculture sector. He further stressed the need for a global mapping of skill requirements to ensure better alignment with international opportunities and future needs.

The Secretaries shared their experiences and perspectives on various initiatives and challenges in their respective domains. The Prime Minister shared his suggestions and his vision for the future course of action. The meeting was marked by comprehensive and productive discussions across the sectors, focusing on effective implementation, greater convergence and accelerated progress towards the goals of Viksit Bharat.

The meeting was attended by the Cabinet Secretary, Secretaries of key Ministries as well as senior officials from the Prime Minister's Office.

2287943.title: India hosts BRICS Network University Conference and the International Governing Board Meeting, strengthening BRICS Higher Education Cooperation
2287943.body_html:
Ministry of Education
India hosts BRICS Network University Conference and the International Governing Board Meeting, strengthening BRICS Higher Education Cooperation
Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems proposed as a new thematic area under the BRICS Network University
International governing board adopts declaration and advances academic cooperation
Posted On: 22 JUL 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

As part of India's BRICS Presidency 2026, the Union Ministry of Education successfully convened the International Governing Board (IGB) meeting of the BRICS Network University (BRICS NU) on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) in virtual mode, following the BRICS Network University Conference on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems held on Monday (July 20, 2026). The two-day engagement brought together government representatives, university leaders, academics and experts from BRICS member countries to strengthen collaboration in higher education, research and innovation.

The IGB meeting was inaugurated by the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Education, Dr. K. M. Praphullachandra Sharma, while Dean (International Relations), IIT Bombay, Prof. Sudarshan Kumar, presented an overview of the BRICS Network University, its expanding institutional network and ongoing collaborative initiatives. Member countries also shared updates on their participating universities and academic cooperation activities undertaken during the past year.

Representatives from the BRICS member countries, including Brazil, China, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates, along with university leaders, academics and experts, delivered country interventions showcasing national initiatives and best practices. The deliberations reaffirmed the collective commitment to strengthening the BRICS Network University through enhanced academic cooperation, collaborative research, institutional partnerships and knowledge exchange.

A key highlight of the meeting was the presentation of the outcomes of the BRICS Network University Conference on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems, the first conference of its kind under the BRICS NU framework. The conference deliberated on the mapping, documentation, preservation and responsible digital dissemination of traditional and indigenous knowledge systems, while emphasizing ethical governance, community ownership, equitable benefit-sharing and the responsible use of emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence. The Conference also developed Guiding Principles on Strengthening Academic Collaboration on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems for consideration by the International Governing Board.

Recognising the significance of this emerging area of cooperation, the International Governing Board deliberated on the proposal to include Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems as a new International Thematic Group (ITG) under the BRICS Network University. The proposal received broad support from member countries and marks an important milestone towards institutionalising collaboration on traditional knowledge within the BRICS higher education framework. Member countries agreed to continue consultations on the concept note with a view to advancing the proposal.

The Governing Board also reviewed the BRICS Network University Action Plan (2025–2028), discussed the development of the new BRICS NU website, considered measures to enhance institutional cooperation, academic mobility and collaborative research, and adopted the BRICS Network University International Governing Board Declaration after detailed deliberations.

The meeting reaffirmed the collective commitment of BRICS member countries to strengthening the BRICS Network University as a leading platform for higher education, research, innovation and people-to-people exchanges. India thanked all participating delegations for their constructive engagement and reiterated its commitment to advancing academic cooperation under the theme of its BRICS Presidency, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability."
